extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent prosecutors, patent attorneys, USPTO officials, and policymakers working with U.S. patent practice
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts the statutory standards and procedural requirements from the Leahy–Smith America Invents Act (AIA) governing patentability, filing formalities, derivation/derived-patent remedies, and related USPTO procedures in U.S. law. Targets requirements that determine whether patents may be obtained, maintained, challenged, or corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory definitions (inventor, joint inventor, joint research agreement, effective filing date, claimed invention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides definitions used throughout the Act: 'inventor' means the individual (or individuals for joint invention) who invented or discovered the subject matter; 'joint inventor'/'coinventor' means any one of the individuals who invented or discovered the subject matter of a joint invention; 'joint research agreement' means a written contract, grant, or cooperative agreement entered into by two or more persons or entities for performance of experimental, developmental, or research work in the field of the claimed invention; 'effective filing date' defined by actual filing date or the earliest application to which priority/benefit is claimed under sections 119, 365(a)/(b), 120, 121, or 365(c); 'claimed invention' means the subject matter defined by a claim in a patent or application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutory definitions control how later sections (e.g., prior art, derivation, common ownership) are applied. Effective filing date rules include benefit/priority claims and reissue determinations (e.g., application for reissue deemed to have claim contained in original patent).

rubrics_metrics.name: §102 — Conditions for patentability; novelty (prior art bars)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person is entitled to a patent unless: (1) the claimed invention was patented, described in a printed publication, in public use, on sale, or otherwise available to the public before the effective filing date; or (2) the claimed invention was described in a patent issued under section 151, or in an application for patent published/ deemed published under §122(b), that names another inventor and was effectively filed before the effective filing date of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the fundamental novelty / prior-art exclusion. 'Otherwise available to the public' covers broad disclosure modes. Clause (2) addresses prior-filed patents/applications naming another inventor (intervening patents/applications). Later subsections (b)-(d) provide statutory exceptions and rules about effective filing dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: §102(b)(1) — One-year grace-period exception for disclosures ≤1 year before effective filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: A disclosure made 1 year or less before the effective filing date is not prior art under §102(a)(1) if: (A) the disclosure was made by the inventor or joint inventor or by another who obtained the subject matter directly or indirectly from the inventor or joint inventor; or (B) the subject matter disclosed had, before such disclosure, been publicly disclosed by the inventor or joint inventor or another who obtained it directly or indirectly from the inventor or joint inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes a limited inventor-originated grace period. Disclosures by third parties that derive the information from the inventor are treated as non‑prior art if within one year. The one-year timing is measured against the effective filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: §102(b)(2) — Exceptions for disclosures appearing in prior applications or patents
rubrics_metrics.description: A disclosure in a patent or published application is not prior art under §102(a)(2) if: (A) the subject matter disclosed was obtained directly or indirectly from the inventor or joint inventor; (B) the subject matter had, before it was effectively filed, been publicly disclosed by the inventor or joint inventor or another who obtained it directly or indirectly from the inventor or joint inventor; or (C) the subject matter disclosed and the claimed invention were owned by the same person or subject to an obligation of assignment to the same person not later than the effective filing date of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides carve-outs so that an earlier-filed patent/application will not bar patentability if the earlier disclosure derived from the applicant or if there is common ownership/assignment (subject to conditions in (C)).

rubrics_metrics.name: §102(c) — Common ownership rule under joint research agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter disclosed and a claimed invention shall be deemed owned by the same person (for purposes of §102(b)(2)(C)) if: (1) the subject matter disclosed was developed and the claimed invention was made by, or on behalf of, one or more parties to a joint research agreement in effect on or before the effective filing date; (2) the claimed invention was made as a result of activities within the scope of the joint research agreement; and (3) the application for patent for the claimed invention discloses or is amended to disclose the names of the parties to the joint research agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves CREATE-act style common-ownership protections for collaborative research when the statutory conditions (including disclosure of parties) are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: §102(d) — Effective filing date rules for patents and published applications as prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: For determining whether a patent or application is prior art under §102(a)(2), the patent or application shall be considered to have been effectively filed as of its actual filing date, or if entitled to priority/benefit under §§119/365/120/121/365(c), as of the filing date of the earliest such application that describes the subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This specifies how priority/benefit claims change the effective filing date of earlier patents/applications for prior-art determinations—important when evaluating intervening patents/applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: §103 — Conditions for patentability; non-obviousness
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent may not be obtained if differences between the claimed invention and the prior art are such that the claimed invention as a whole would have been obvious before the effective filing date to a person having ordinary skill in the art to which the claimed invention pertains. Patentability shall not be negated by the manner in which the invention was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard statutory non-obviousness test anchored to a hypothetical person having ordinary skill in the art (PHOSITA). The Act clarifies that how the inventor arrived at the invention is not determinative of patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeal of statutory invention registration and foreign-invention restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act repeals §157 (statutory invention registration) and repeals §104 (requirements for inventions made abroad). Conforming amendments remove cross-references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removes the SIR option and eliminates older statutory bars tied to inventions made abroad—affects what filings/options are available and which prior-law rules apply to older filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: §291 — Derived patents (civil relief for derivation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner of a patent may have relief by civil action against the owner of another patent that claims the same invention and has an earlier effective filing date if the invention claimed in such other patent was derived from the inventor of the invention claimed in the complaining patent. An action may be filed only before the end of the one-year period beginning on the date of issuance of the first patent containing a claim to the allegedly derived invention and naming the individual alleged to have derived such invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates a civil remedy for derivation and imposes a strict one-year filing limitation tied to issuance of the first patent naming the alleged derived inventor.

rubrics_metrics.name: §135 — Derivation proceedings (PTAB institution and petition requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may file a petition to institute a derivation proceeding in the Office. The petition must set forth with particularity the basis for finding that an inventor named in an earlier application derived the claimed invention from an inventor named in the petitioner's application and, without authorization, the earlier application was filed. Any such petition may be filed only within the one-year period beginning on the date of the first publication of a claim to the same or substantially the same invention, shall be made under oath, and shall be supported by substantial evidence. The Director may institute a derivation proceeding; the Director's institution decision is final and nonappealable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High pleading standard ('with particularity') plus evidentiary support and strict time windows; institution is discretionary but final as to institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB conduct and remedies in derivation proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: In a derivation proceeding, the Patent Trial and Appeal Board shall determine whether an inventor named in the earlier application derived the claimed invention from the petitioner and, without authorization, the earlier application was filed. The Board may correct inventor naming, defer action for certain periods (e.g., 3-month delay after Director issues a patent including the claimed invention), stay proceedings pending other chapter 30/31/32 proceedings, and final adverse Board decisions constitute final refusal or cancellation of claims. Parties may settle by written statement (subject to Board review) and may choose arbitration under specified conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides procedural mechanisms (deferral, stay, settlement, arbitration) and strong remedies (cancellation/correction) for proven derivation; requires regulations prescribing standards and evidence rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elimination of interferences; creation/role of Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory references to 'Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences' are replaced by 'Patent Trial and Appeal Board'; 'interference' language is replaced by 'derivation proceeding'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transforms prior 'interference' procedures (first-to-invent era) into derivation/ PTAB framework consistent with first-inventor-to-file regime; affects appeal and review provisions and cross-references throughout Title 35.

rubrics_metrics.name: §115 — Inventor’s oath or declaration; naming inventor and required statements
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed under §111(a) or commencing national stage under §371 must include or be amended to include the name of the inventor for any claimed invention. Each individual who is the inventor or joint inventor must execute an oath or declaration. The oath/declaration must state that (1) the application was made or authorized by the affiant or declarant, and (2) the individual believes themselves to be the original inventor or an original joint inventor of a claimed invention in the application. The Director may specify additional inventor/invention information required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing formalities require inventor-identifying statements; the Director has regulatory authority to specify additional required information; required statements can be included in assignments in certain circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute statement in lieu of inventor's oath/declaration (§115(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may file a substitute statement instead of an oath/declaration when the individual is: (A) deceased, (B) under legal incapacity, (C) cannot be found or reached after diligent effort, or (D) is under an obligation to assign but refuses to make the oath/declaration. The substitute statement must identify the individual, set forth the circumstances permitting the substitute, and contain any additional information required by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows prosecution to proceed when an inventor cannot personally sign; strict content and circumstance requirements; Director may expand permitted circumstances by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: §115 — Assignment and earlier-filed application exceptions; copies and evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual under obligation to assign may include the required statements in the assignment instead of separate filing. Requirements under §115 do not apply to an individual with respect to a later application if an earlier-filed application (to which benefit/priority is claimed) included an oath/declaration, substitute statement, or qualifying assignment; the Director may require copies of the earlier-filed executed documents to be included in the later application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits reliance on earlier-filed filings for formal compliance but authorizes the Office to demand copies to verify compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental/corrected inventor statements and savings clause (§115(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person making a required statement may withdraw, replace, or otherwise correct the statement at any time. Director shall establish regulations for filing additional statements when naming of inventors changes. If a correctable failure to comply occurs and is remedied per these rules, the patent shall not be invalid or unenforceable for that failure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides remedial mechanisms to cure oath/declaration defects and protects patent validity when remedied according to regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: §115(i) — Acknowledgment of penalties for false statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any declaration or statement filed pursuant to §115 must contain acknowledgment that willful false statements are punishable under 18 U.S.C. §1001 by fine or imprisonment up to 5 years, or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as deterrent and basis for criminal penalties for willful misstatements in inventor declarations/substitute statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statute-of-limitations amendment for Office misconduct proceedings (amendment to §32)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings under §32 shall be commenced not later than the earlier of: (A) 10 years after the date on which the misconduct forming the basis occurred, or (B) 1 year after the date on which the misconduct is made known to an officer or employee of the Office as prescribed in regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes both an absolute 10-year limit and a 1-year discoverability-triggered limit for Office misconduct actions; Director must report biennially on incidents made known but barred by time limitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date and applicability of first-inventor-to-file regime
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as otherwise provided, the amendments converting the U.S. to 'first-inventor-to-file' take effect upon expiration of the 18-month period beginning on enactment and apply to applications/patents that contain claims with effective filing dates on or after that effective date or specific references under §§120, 121, or 365(c) to patents/applications containing such claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transitional rules specify which prior-law provisions continue to apply in particular cases and provide phased applicability tied to effective filing dates and priority references.

rubrics_metrics.name: §33 — Limitation on issuance of patents (human organism exclusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, no patent may issue on a claim directed to or encompassing a human organism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absolute statutory bar on claims directed to or encompassing human organisms; applies to applications pending on or filed on or after enactment and does not affect patents issued on earlier applications to which the subsection does not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority examination for important technologies (authority to prioritize examination)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may, subject to conditions prescribed and at the request of an applicant, provide for prioritization of examination of applications for products, processes, or technologies important to the national economy or national competitiveness, without recovering aggregate extra costs of providing such prioritization (notwithstanding §41 or other law).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits a program for prioritized examination of applications deemed important to national interests; subject to Director-prescribed conditions and policy judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of 60-day period for patent term extension (business day rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: For determining the date on which a product receives permission under second-sentence permission rules, if the permission is transmitted after 4:30 P.M. Eastern Time on a business day, or transmitted on a non-business day, the product is deemed to receive permission on the next business day. 'Business day' defined as Mon–Fri excluding legal holidays under §6103 of title 5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural rule for timing calculations relevant to patent term extension filings and deadlines; applies to pending and subsequent applications subject to extension review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reports, studies, and data-collection requirements affecting policy (prior user rights, small business effects, GAO study of litigation, genetic testing, diversity of applicants)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director and other agencies are required to conduct several studies and issue reports: (a) report on prior user rights in selected industrialized countries (within 4 months); (b) a study of effects on small businesses of eliminating dates of invention and other studies (timelines specified); (c) GAO study of consequences of litigation by non-practicing entities (1-year report); (d) study on genetic testing and independent confirming testing (9-month report); (e) establish methods to study diversity of applicants (within 6 months), etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These mandated studies and reports inform future rulemaking and policy; while not direct patentability criteria, they set expectations for Office action, potential changes, and areas the Office must monitor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivation-related time and evidence standards (institution, deferral, stays, settlements, arbitration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Derivation petitions must be supported by substantial evidence and filed within statutory windows; the Director's institution decision is final and nonappealable; PTAB may defer or stay actions (including waiting 3 months after the Director issues a patent containing the claimed invention), may accept settlements (subject to consistency with record), and parties may elect arbitration under Title 9 rules with notice to Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes tight timeframes, evidentiary thresholds, finality of institution, and multiple procedural mechanisms to resolve derivation disputes while coordinating with parallel proceedings.
